Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Feature parity during tier downgrade - migration questions

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We like Redwood's performance but the finance team is asking if we can safely move from a mid-tier (Throughput) to a compact tier for an interim period without losing a set of critical features. Specifically:

- Can we keep our custom reranker and embeddings behaviour when we drop to Compact for 60 days?
- What happens to feature flags and experiments — are they preserved or do we need a migration window?
- Will there be any prorated credits or one-off concessions if we do a temporary downgrade and then return to Throughput?

I've attached a short spec of our current usage and the features we consider "must keep". We're trying to avoid an engineering-intensive migration if possible.

Can you outline the recommended approach and the tradeoffs? If useful, we can hop on a 30-min call.

Thanks,
Priya Reddy

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Feature parity during tier downgrade - migration questions

Lauren / Kim / Priya — thanks for the clear specification, Priya. High-level options (tradeoffs and ops impact):

1) Feature-preserve via add-on entitlements (recommended minimal lift)
   - We keep the customer on Compact for base throughput/cost but enable a "reranker+embeddings" add-on that pins the model and inference path.
   - Engineering impact: near-zero on Sagewell side; Redwood enables routing and entitlement checks.
   - Cost: add-on priced at ~30% of the Throughput delta (negotiable).
   - Rollback: Immediately reversible; returning to Throughput simply removes the add-on and resumes native entitlements.

2) Temporary model-variant shim (lower latency, more infra work)
   - Recreate the reranker as a lightweight variant tuned for Compact (requires alignment work and QA).
   - Engineering impact: 1-2 sprints on Redwood + lightweight config on Sagewell.
   - Cost: lower per-token cost but upfront engineering time; better for longer downgrades (>90 days).

3) Full downgrade with migration window and prorated credits
   - If features cannot be preserved, offer a one-time credit to cover migration effort + a prorated usage credit for the downgrade window.
   - Typical concession: 15-25% of monthly committed spend for a single-month migration; for 60-day windows we recommend a 20% credit + a guaranteed re-onboarding pathway.

Suggested path for Sagewell (fastest path, balances cost + risk):
- Start Compact + enable add-on for reranker+embeddings for 60 days.
- Redwood to provide a 30% discount on the add-on for the first 60 days as a goodwill concession, conditional on a signed return-to-Throughput commitment (date-locked).
- We will run a short smoke test on day 2 and provide an ops rollback plan.

Operational notes:
- Entitlement: feature flags are preserved in our control plane as flags, but the mapping to plan entitlements must be pinned when add-on is provisioned.
- Metrics: we will snapshot QoE (latency, tokens/sec) before downgrade and again at day 7 to ensure parity.

Links / items I've queued:
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/SAGE-459
- Draft concession doc (internal): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cSagewellMigration

Kim, pricing aside, do we have flexibility on the 30% add-on discount for the first 60 days?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Priya Reddy <ops@sagewell.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Feature parity during tier downgrade - migration questions

Priya — looping back with a recommended approach and next steps. Summary:

- We can enable a "reranker+embeddings" add-on while Sagewell runs Compact for 60 days. That preserves feature parity without any heavy lift on your side.
- Redwood will treat the first 60 days of that add-on as a promotional period at a 30% discount, conditional on a signed plan to return to Throughput by 2027-01-15 (we can mark a soft commitment in the deal).
- We'll snapshot performance on day 0 and day 7; if there's a regression we have an immediate rollback path.

Next steps:
1) Priya: confirm that a 60-day window is acceptable and that Sagewell is comfortable with the return-by date.
2) Ben + Kim: I'll draft a short concession amendment (SAGE-459) and send a signature-ready DocuSign linked to the HubSpot deal.
3) Ops: we'll run a short smoke test on day 2 and share results.

Would you be available for a 30-min alignment call tomorrow at 11:00 AM PT? If so, I will send a calendar invite and include a one-page concession summary.

Thanks — will push the concession draft once I have Priya's confirmation.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, GTM Solutions
Redwood Inference
